crates/app/src/daily_task_marker.rs:
- write_marker_in(base, task, date_ist, keep_days: i64) -> std::io::Result<MarkerDurability>, with pub enum MarkerDurability { Durable, RenamedNotDirSynced }. The body runs inside tickvault_storage::off_worker::off_worker, as today.
  (a) Note whether base exists, then create_dir_all(base).
  (b) Open the fixed path <task>-<date>.marker.tmp with OpenOptions create+write+truncate, so a crash leftover is overwritten. write_all the unchanged contents 'build=<sha>\ndelivered_date_ist=<date>\n', then sync_all.
  (c) rename(tmp, final). An error in (a)–(c) returns Err.
  (d) Open base and sync_all it; also sync its parent if (a) created base. A failure here returns Ok(RenamedNotDirSynced), never Err.
  (e) Sweep after Ok; sweep errors are ignored, as today.
  The doc states the limit: only base and at most its parent are synced.
- marker_exists_in: still off_worker and still fail-open (any error reads false). It opens the file, reads through Read::take(4096), and returns true only if some line equals exactly 'delivered_date_ist=<date>'. Empty, torn, wrong-date and unreadable files read false; the legacy two-line format still passes.
- sweep_old_markers_in(base, task, date, keep_days): cutoff = date - keep_days instead of the constant. Also removes same-task '<task>-<date>.marker.tmp' files older than the cutoff. Foreign and unparsable names are still kept.
- Public API:
  - pub fn try_write_daily_marker(task, date) -> io::Result<MarkerDurability>, keeping DAILY_MARKER_SWEEP_DAYS (7);
  - pub fn try_write_daily_marker_keeping(task, date, keep_days) -> io::Result<MarkerDurability>.
  - REMOVE pub fn write_daily_marker, so no caller can drop a result.
  - No bare #[must_use]: clippy::double_must_use fires on io::Result under -D warnings.
  - Update the module doc: atomic write, strict reader, per-task keep horizon.

crates/app/src/dhan_live_crossverify_boot.rs:
- Import change: use crate::daily_task_marker::{daily_marker_exists, daily_marker_path, try_write_daily_marker_keeping, MarkerDurability}.
- pub const CROSSVERIFY_MARKER_KEEP_DAYS: i64 = 400, with const _: () = assert!(CROSSVERIFY_MARKER_KEEP_DAYS > 90 + tickvault_storage::partition_archive::MAX_CROSSVERIFY_HOLD_DAYS). MAX_CROSSVERIFY_HOLD_DAYS = 3 is pub at partition_archive.rs:1319 (Verified).
- Pure pub fn crossverify_marker_keep_is_short(gated_hot_days_max: u32) -> bool: true when gated_hot_days_max + MAX_CROSSVERIFY_HOLD_DAYS + 3 >= KEEP. main.rs calls it just before spawn_dhan_live_crossverify (main.rs ~3602), passing max(config.partition_retention.retention_days, market_data_hot_days, depth_hot_days, intraday_hot_days). pressure_hot_days is EXCLUDED because that leg is ungated. On true it emits one warn!(code = ErrorCode::WsGapConnectionState.code_str(), source = "xverify_marker_keep_short"). The raw configured days are used because partition_archive::effective_hot_days is pub(crate). Assumed: its floor never lifts a value near 397; confirm at implementation.
- AttemptFailure gains MarkerNotWritten => "marker_not_written" and AuditRowsLost => "audit_rows_lost".
- persist_report is split:
  - fn persist_report_into(writer: &mut DhanLiveXverifyAuditWriter, report, day_start_ist_nanos, tolerance_paise, batch_rows: usize) -> PersistOutcome;
  - a thin persist_report(questdb, ...) that builds the writer with ::new and passes PERSIST_BATCH_ROWS.
  - pub struct PersistOutcome { final_flush_ok, daily_appended, rows_discarded, rows_flushed, cell_append_errors, tape_append_errors }.
  - flush_if_full records before = w.pending(). On Err it adds `before` to rows_discarded; flush() discards on every Err (Verified, persistence.rs ~926-957). On Ok with pending()==0 it adds `before` to rows_flushed. The final flush is counted the same way.
  - XVERIFY_PERSIST_ROWS_COUNTER increments by rows_flushed ONLY. Today it counts findings + tape + 1 even after a mid-run discard (Verified).
  - The xverify_persist_partial and xverify_persist_failed error! lines keep their code and source. Each gains a rows_discarded field and text saying the S3 hold stays and the attempt will retry.
- Pure pub fn persist_verdict(&PersistOutcome) -> Result<(), AttemptFailure>:
  - NotPersisted if !final_flush_ok || !daily_appended;
  - else AuditRowsLost if rows_discarded > 0, cell_append_errors > 0 or tape_append_errors > 0;
  - else Ok.
- classify_attempt(vacuous, measured, persist: Result<(), AttemptFailure>, complete). Order: Vacuous, then !measured -> Incomplete, then persist Err (its own variant), then !complete -> Incomplete. should_write_marker keeps its signature and is called with persist.is_ok(). The debug_assert_eq agreement stays.
- fn record_day(today) -> Result<(), AttemptFailure> is the ONLY marker-write site and calls try_write_daily_marker_keeping(CROSSVERIFY_MARKER_TASK, today, CROSSVERIFY_MARKER_KEEP_DAYS):
  - Ok(Durable): the existing info 'recorded' line, then Ok.
  - Ok(RenamedNotDirSynced): warn!(code = WsGapConnectionState, source = "xverify_marker_dir_sync_failed"), the same info line, then Ok.
  - Err(err): warn!(code = WsGapConnectionState, source = "xverify_attempt_marker_write_failed", ?err, path = %daily_marker_path(..).display()), then Err(MarkerNotWritten).
- run_once's Ok arm returns record_day(today).
- Pure pub fn next_attempt_kind(prev: Option<AttemptFailure>) -> AttemptKind { Full, MarkerOnly }: MarkerOnly iff prev == Some(MarkerNotWritten). run_day keeps the previous attempt's failure. A MarkerOnly attempt calls record_day(today) only: no wait_for_jwt, no run_cross_verification, no persist, and divergence_paged is not touched. Attempt count, 900 s spacing, XVERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_DAY and the retry_delay_secs fit are unchanged. run_option_pass still runs once after the loop.
- report_final_failure stays exhaustive:
  - MarkerNotWritten gets its own error! arm with the literal source = "xverify_failed", and text: 'comparison finished and every row was accepted by the database, but the day marker could not be saved to disk; today's S3 archive stays held; check disk space and permissions on the state folder'.
  - AuditRowsLost joins the existing NoToken | RunFailed | NotPersisted | Incomplete arm.
- Doc comment on persist_option_findings: it keeps its discard-then-succeed shape on purpose, because it writes no marker and never pages (§12.15.6).

(1) no-rest full file, new §12.15.7 'the day marker means what it says':
- 'Persisted' means every finding, tape row and daily row was ACKed, with zero rows discarded or refused.
- The marker counts only after tmp, fsync, rename, and a strict content read.
- A marker write failure is a failed attempt. It is retried marker-only and paged only after the last attempt, on the existing xverify_failed source.
- Crossverify markers are kept 400 days.
- Amend the §12.15.5 REJECT row to: '...writes the marker on any condition other than classify_attempt returning Ok in the same attempt, or in the immediately previous same-process attempt when that attempt failed only with MarkerNotWritten'.
- Honest limits:
  - an ACK means accepted into the WAL, not applied;
  - only base and its parent directory are fsynced;
  - markers already swept cannot be recovered;
  - MarketData-class tables (hot window 15 days, longer than the 3-day hold) can only Proceed or Override.
- REJECT rows: a unit-returning marker write; an is_file()-only reader; a sweep horizon shorter than the gated hold lookback; counting a discarded row as persisted.

prs.title: fix(xverify): every attempt ends by 17:23 under a timeout, before the 17:25 scheduled stop, and the last attempt is decided once
prs.scope:
Sources: xv-missing-run §A (time bounds, attempt_budget_secs, timeout) and xv-read-too-early §C1 (last attempt decided once, conservatively). Boot module only.

The defect is Verified: retry_delay_secs bounds an attempt's end at EVENING_STOP 17:30 (62,700 + 300), but shutdown_class::SCHEDULED_STOP_WINDOW_START_SECS_OF_DAY_IST is 62,700, which is 17:25 (shutdown_class.rs:49). So a final attempt can be killed mid-run.

crates/app/src/dhan_live_crossverify_boot.rs:
- XVERIFY_DEADLINE_SECS_OF_DAY_IST = SCHEDULED_STOP_WINDOW_START - 60 = 62,640 (17:24).
- XVERIFY_LAST_END_SECS_OF_DAY_IST = DEADLINE - 60 = 62,580 (17:23).
- XVERIFY_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECS: 900 -> 760.
- const asserts:
  - RUN_SECS (56,460) + attempt_max_secs(600) (960) + 3 × (760 + 960) <= LAST_END. This is exactly 62,580.
  - LAST_END < DEADLINE < SCHEDULED_STOP_WINDOW_START < EVENING_STOP.
- retry_delay_secs and option_pass_fits bound on LAST_END.
- Pure pub fn attempt_budget_secs(now, config_budget) -> Option<u64>:
  - min(config_budget, LAST_END - now - token wait (300) - PERSIST_MARGIN_SECS);
  - None if the result is below 120 s, which logs warn source xverify_attempt_skipped_no_time.
  - A shrunk budget is passed to run_cross_verification through a cloned config. A run cut short ends budget_elapsed, which is Incomplete, so no marker.
- Every attempt is wrapped in tokio::time::timeout(attempt_max_secs(budget)). On elapse: warn!(code = WsGapConnectionState, source = "xverify_attempt_timed_out"), Err(Incomplete).
- run_day computes is_last = retry_delay_secs(attempts, start + attempt_max, attempt_max).is_none() BEFORE each attempt and uses that same value afterwards: final report if true, sleep if false. PR 1's MarkerOnly attempts use the same rule.
prs.excludes: Not in this PR: readiness (PR 4), catch-up, wake rule and supervisor (PR 7), and any alarm or phrase change. No new sources are filtered.

prs.title: fix(xverify): a failed fetch no longer hides a real divergence, and the end-of-session excuse is derived and never Clean
prs.scope:
Sources: xv-missing-minutes-page A1 (verdict order, without its gates) and xv-read-too-early §A plus §C3 (derived late window, LateWindowPolicy). Pure comparison and persistence only.

The defect is Verified at dhan_live_crossverify.rs:1067: `if degraded { Partial } else if real { Diverged }`.

crates/app/src/dhan_feed_stack.rs: CATCHUP_LATENESS_MARGIN_SECS (line 7000) and MEASURED_MAX_DELIVERY_LAG_SECS (line 7018) become pub(crate). Visibility only.

crates/app/src/dhan_live_crossverify.rs:
- Delete TAIL_UNSEALED_MINUTES (line 148).
- LATE_SEAL_WINDOW_MINUTES = (CATCHUP_LATENESS_MARGIN_SECS + 60).div_ceil(60). That is 5 today, covering 15:35-15:39. Const assert: × 60 >= margin.
- is_tail_minute becomes pub fn is_late_window_minute(minute, day_start, sealed_through_secs_of_day: Option<i64>), O(1). None means the last LATE_SEAL_WINDOW_MINUTES of the session.
- compare_day_in_scope replaces `degraded: bool` with inputs: VerdictInputs { rest_incomplete: bool, missing: MissingJudgeable, late: LateWindowPolicy }.
  - MissingJudgeable: Copy enum {Judged, LiveTruncated}. PR 4 adds NotReady.
  - LateWindowPolicy: {Strict, Excuse{sealed_through_secs_of_day: Option<i64>}}.
- Verdict:
  - judged = missing == Judged.
  - real = cells_diverged > 0 || (judged && (missing_live_traded > 0 || missing_live_index > 0)).
  - real -> Diverged.
  - else rest_incomplete, !judged, missing_rest > 0, late_excused > 0 or missing_live_unjudged > 0 -> Partial.
  - else Clean.
  - Vacuous outcomes are unchanged.
- Why this is sound: a target whose vendor fetch failed has no vendor bars, so it can add only missing_rest, never a false missing_live. A truncated live read (ORDER BY ts ASC LIMIT cuts the end) is the one input that can fake missing_live, so it alone disables missing judging.
- New DayComparison fields: missing_live_late, late_excused, missing_live_unjudged, missing_judgeable. New CellKind values: LateExcused and MissingLiveUnjudged. tail_unsealed / TailUnsealed are kept and written as 0, with a dated note.
- The test helper compare_day keeps `degraded: bool`, mapped to rest_incomplete + Judged + Strict, so its ~45 call sites stay.
- run_cross_verification passes rest_incomplete = budget_elapsed || rest_failures > 0, missing = LiveTruncated when live_truncated, and Excuse{None} (the interim default until PR 4).

- New cell-kind symbols. DEDUP unchanged.

**Claims I checked:**
1. **Candidate 1 is wrong about where `wal_tables` lives.** It says the watcher's `WalTableRow` has only `name` and `suspended`. False: `wal_suspension_watcher.rs:132` already carries `writer_txn` and `sequencer_txn`, and `partition_archive` imports that row type at line 120. So candidate 2's placement wins: move `fetch_wal_tables` into `wal_suspension_watcher` and add `wal_applied_through` next to the parser and row type. `wal_apply_verdict` is unchanged. (PR 4)

I took candidate 2's plumbing instead: a `static CATCHUP_PROGRESS` plus a `&'static` field with a `#[cfg(test)]` override. I kept candidate 1's semantics: publish the completed sweep's floor cutoff, which an overrun never raises. (PR 4)

So the scheduled stop can kill a final attempt mid-run. Candidate 1 left this until PR 6. Arithmetic checked: 56,460 + 960 + 3 × 1,720 = 62,580.
